text:
marina: Quick note - rolled Ivy-9B (int4) into a tiny canary. Seeing p99 tail spikes (~18%) vs our 9B baseline for short chat.

sanjay: p95 OK, p99 spikes line up with kv cache misses and large memcpy durations.

lucas: paste small log snippet?

marina: log:
```
[2026-03-21T10:02:01Z] w-2 | req=aa1 batch=6 max_new_tokens=64
[2026-03-21T10:02:01Z] w-2 | kv_miss shard=1 try=1
[2026-03-21T10:02:01Z] w-2 | memcpy 28ms compute 17ms total p99 118ms
[2026-03-21T10:02:01Z] w-2 | OOM-fallback reclaimed=88MB
```

marta: looks like fragmentation + prefetch allocations. Are int4 prefetches on?

marina: yes default prefetch=on. I flipped prefetch off on a node slice; p99 dropped ~10ms.

sanjay: propose two quick ablations on prod-sampled replay:
- Config X: prefetch=false, max_batch=4, slot_reserve_mb=128, eviction_threshold=0.65
- Config Y: prefetch=true, max_batch=3, warmup_reserve_mb=256 for 20s, eviction_threshold=0.75

deploy-bot: config X deployed to canary-group-gamma.

marina: X run (30m) summary uploaded.

marta: X results: p99 -12ms, OOM fallbacks -70%, small QA EM drop ~0.6%.

marina: launching Y now.

deploy-bot: Y run complete.

lucas: Y results: p99 -7ms, OOM fallbacks -42%, QA stable.

sanjay: tradeoff - X better latency but minor QA regression; Y safer. Suggest make Y default canary and run a 24h X variant with max_new_tokens_default=96 to test QA recovery.

marta: +1. I'll open runtime bug for memcpy spike paths (ticket RI-2026-ivy-copy).

marina: updated model catalog draft: default canary profile = prefetch=on, max_batch=3, eviction=0.75, warmup_reserve=256MB. Starting 24h X-run now.
